title: Liquid Close-Up Photos in a Cleaning and Damage Fees Approval Set
content:
**Rule.** The liquid close-ups of a Cleaning and Damage Fees approval photo set are read from the incident category and the reported trip's actual duration: a food or drink spill or bodily fluids on a trip whose actual duration reached the long-trip minutes adds the long-exposure close-ups; a food or drink spill or bodily fluids on a shorter trip, or animal hair or mess or smoke or vape odor, adds the short-exposure close-ups; any other incident adds no liquid close-ups.

The long-trip minutes are 30 minutes; the long-exposure close-ups are 2 photos and the short-exposure close-ups are 1 photo, and they are added to the approval photo set. The actual duration is the trip's actual minutes on the trip record in Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares); the incident category is the one on the assessment.

**Evidence reviewers' questions**

*Does a trip of exactly 30 minutes count as reaching the long-trip minutes?* Yes; 30 minutes or more adds 2 long-exposure close-ups to a spill or bodily fluids report. A trip of 29 minutes is shorter and adds 1.

*Does the trip's duration change the close-ups for animal hair or mess, or for smoke or vape odor?* No; those add 1 short-exposure close-up whatever the duration.

*Which incidents add no liquid close-ups?* Any incident outside those named — trash or debris, interior damage and exterior damage.

| Incident category | Trip's actual duration | Liquid close-ups |
|---|---|---|
| food or drink spill, or bodily fluids | 30 minutes or more | 2 |
| food or drink spill, or bodily fluids | under 30 minutes | 1 |
| animal hair or mess, or smoke or vape odor | any | 1 |
| trash or debris, interior damage, exterior damage | any | none |
